lessons: The fence leaves out chupa/daemon.py, but the change forces it. daemon.py:502 builds Scheduler from journal and callables only, with no repo access. scheduler.py therefore cannot read the committed ticket.md sha that drain.premise_parked needs. Add chupa/daemon.py to the fence.

Give Scheduler an injected callable, built in daemon.py from repo through the git seam, that returns a stem's committed ticket.md sha. Do not derive the repo from the journal or state dir: a configured state_dir breaks that, and it bypasses the git seam.

Hold a stem in serve only when its last state is premise_failed and drain.premise_parked reports it parked at the sha that callable returns. Reuse premise_parked and do not add a second park check, as the ticket requires.

After amending the fence, run chupa review review-before-dispatch. Fix every finding until it approves, including tests that build Scheduler directly and must pass the new callable. All of tests is already fenced.
